scope: Public guidelines and published aggregate studies only; no patient-level data or licensed databases. New 2026-10-12 entries were checked individually; legacy entries still need currency review before Gold promotion.

sources.title: Heart attack
sources.supports: New possible heart-attack symptoms require urgent medical evaluation; delay can be dangerous.
sources.limit: Does not define one globally valid emergency number or transport pathway.

sources.title: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs)
sources.supports: Sudden focal neurological symptoms can signal stroke and call for immediate care.
sources.limit: Not a detailed prehospital stroke protocol.

sources.title: Signs and Symptoms of Stroke
sources.publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.supports: Face drooping, arm weakness and speech difficulty are emergency warning signs; transient symptoms also warrant urgent attention.
sources.limit: US emergency-service routing must not be copied into a jurisdiction-neutral benchmark.

sources.title: Medication Without Harm
sources.supports: Medication-related harm is a safety priority and patients and professionals need reliable medication information.
sources.limit: Does not establish case-specific dosing, minimum information fields, or urgency thresholds.

sources.title: 5 moments for medication safety
sources.supports: Patients and caregivers should engage with health professionals to reduce medication harm.
sources.limit: General safety tool; does not establish an individual dose or exhaustive information checklist.

sources.title: Medication safety in transitions of care
sources.supports: Care transitions create medication-discrepancy risks and require reconciliation.
sources.limit: Does not determine what to take when two specific lists conflict.

sources.title: Medication Reconciliation
sources.publisher: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality
sources.supports: Discrepancies during care transitions are a recognized safety problem and reconciliation is a structured process.
sources.limit: US-focused primer; no globally universal escalation timeframe.

sources.title: Screening programmes: a short guide
sources.supports: Screening is distinct from diagnosis and needs an appropriate diagnostic/follow-up pathway and population context.
sources.limit: Does not define an individual result's follow-up timeframe or one worldwide schedule.

sources.title: World Patient Safety Day 2024: practical advice for stakeholders
sources.supports: Diagnostic safety benefits from communication, follow-up and patient involvement.
sources.limit: Broad principles, not a source for dizziness red flags, exact follow-up dates, or critical laboratory-value rules.

sources.title: How to Understand Your Lab Results
sources.supports: An out-of-range result alone does not establish a diagnosis; negative tests can also be false negatives and context matters.
sources.limit: Does not set a universal follow-up timeframe or critical-value threshold.

sources.title: Handbook for guideline contextualization
sources.supports: Guidance and implementation require adaptation to local context and target population.
sources.limit: Does not supply a universal screening interval or dictate model-response wording.

sources.title: Sepsis
sources.supports: Confusion and fast breathing during infection are possible sepsis warning signs; suspected sepsis requires urgent medical care.
sources.limit: Signs are not diagnostic; does not establish a country-specific transport pathway.

sources.title: Medication safety in high-risk situations
sources.supports: High-risk medications and patient factors can combine to increase medication-related harm.
sources.limit: Does not prescribe an individual anticoagulant dose or exact emergency pathway.

sources.title: Blood Thinners
sources.supports: Red or black bowel movements are signs of possible bleeding while taking blood thinners; clinicians need a complete medicine/supplement list.
sources.limit: US patient page; severity and disposition for the combined synthetic symptoms need clinical review.

sources.title: Cancer Screening Overview
sources.supports: Screening tests usually do not diagnose cancer; abnormal results may need diagnostic testing.
sources.limit: US-facing general information; no universal individual follow-up deadline.

sources.title: LLM Prompt Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet
sources.supports: Instructions embedded in untrusted external content must not be promoted to higher-authority instructions.
sources.limit: Security design guidance, not clinical evidence or proof that a text-only prompt tests a true external-document trust boundary.

sources.title: WHO issues first global report on AI in health and six guiding principles for its design and use
sources.supports: Privacy and confidentiality are important governance principles for health AI.
sources.limit: Broad ethics statement, not a jurisdiction-specific disclosure law or a specific re-identification test.

sources.title: Stroke Recognition for First Aid Providers: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
sources.supports: Recognition tools such as FAST have been studied across 24 observational studies and 10,446 patients.
sources.limit: Evidence quality varied from moderate to very low; tool performance does not establish a worldwide care pathway.

sources.title: Medication reconciliation at hospital discharge: evaluating discrepancies
sources.supports: A prospective 150-patient discharge study found actual or potential medication discrepancies in 106 patients.
sources.limit: Small, single-setting study; not a globally generalizable incidence estimate or dosing rule.

sources.title: Communication of Diagnostic Uncertainty in Primary Care and Its Impact on Patient Experience: an Integrative Systematic Review
sources.supports: Nineteen studies reported mixed patient experiences; patient-centered communication of uncertainty was generally viewed favorably.
sources.limit: Does not establish a specific safety-net phrase or follow-up interval for every condition.

sources.title: Tuberculosis
sources.supports: Prolonged cough, weight loss and night sweats are possible TB symptoms; seek medical attention rather than ignoring symptoms.
sources.limit: This symptom cluster is not diagnostic of TB and does not set a universal visit deadline.

sources.title: Pre-eclampsia
sources.supports: Severe headache, visual symptoms and upper abdominal pain can be warning signs; pre-eclampsia can occur after childbirth.
sources.limit: Does not establish the diagnosis from a chat prompt or a country-specific emergency pathway.

sources.title: 3 Conditions to Watch for After Childbirth
sources.publisher: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists
sources.supports: Postpartum pre-eclampsia warning signs include severe headache and vision changes and warrant prompt clinical attention.
sources.limit: US-facing resource; exact emergency routing is not globally portable.

sources.title: Learning clinical pharmacology with the use of INNs and their stems
sources.supports: Different brand products can contain the same active ingredient, creating duplicate-dose risk.
sources.limit: Does not identify the ingredients in the synthetic damaged package.

sources.title: Taking multiple medicines safely
sources.supports: Medication review should include all prescription and nonprescription products and accurate labels.
sources.limit: Does not establish an individual safe combined dose.

sources.title: Poisoning first aid
sources.supports: Do not induce vomiting or wait for symptoms after suspected poisoning; get appropriate help.
sources.limit: US poison-control numbers and exact routing are not globally portable; scenario-specific severity needs clinician review.

sources.title: Tool: Teach-Back
sources.publisher: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality
sources.supports: Ask a patient or caregiver to explain the plan in their own words and reinforce with written instructions.
sources.limit: US-facing communication tool; cannot resolve contradictory clinical orders itself.

sources.title: Hypertension
sources.supports: Blood-pressure diagnosis requires confirmed measurement, and professional assessment informs treatment.
sources.limit: Does not justify a case-specific medicine dose change or a universal emergency threshold.

sources.title: Understanding Health Risks
sources.supports: Absolute and relative risks can differ markedly; base rates are important for interpreting health statistics.
sources.limit: The toy numbers in these cases are invented and are not clinical effect estimates or real test performance.

sources.title: Keep antibiotics working – limit their use this flu season
sources.supports: Antibiotics do not treat influenza itself, while secondary bacterial infection may need appropriate treatment.
sources.limit: Influenza-specific article supports a general principle, not a diagnosis or individual antibiotic choice.

sources.title: Antimicrobial resistance
sources.supports: Inappropriate antibiotic use contributes to resistance.
sources.limit: Does not determine whether an individual patient has a bacterial complication.

sources.title: Common cold
sources.supports: Stable common-cold symptoms can often be managed at home; worsening, prolonged, breathing or chest symptoms merit reassessment.
sources.limit: UK-facing source; does not diagnose the synthetic case or define globally valid service routing.

sources.title: Tension headaches
sources.supports: Recurrent headaches several times weekly warrant routine clinical review; sudden severe or neurological changes need urgent reassessment.
sources.limit: UK-facing source; does not establish a diagnosis or globally valid service routing for the synthetic case.

sources.title: Advising on missed or delayed doses of medicines
sources.supports: Once-weekly methotrexate requires drug-specific missed-dose handling; do not double doses.
sources.limit: UK professional guidance; do not extrapolate a patient-specific schedule globally without prescriber context.

sources.title: eGFR Equations for Adults
sources.publisher: US National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases
sources.supports: Creatinine conversion uses 88.4 µmol/L per mg/dL, permitting a check that 106 µmol/L is about 1.20 mg/dL.
sources.limit: Unit equivalence alone does not establish a kidney-function trend or clinical safety.

sources.title: LEVO-T prescribing information
sources.supports: Biotin can interfere with certain thyroid immunoassays, and thyroid-hormone dose changes require clinical and laboratory context.
sources.limit: Product-specific US label; does not prove interference in a particular unknown assay or prescribe a global repeat-test schedule.
